user.title: Add an OpenHydronic board
user.description: Enter the IP address or hostname of the ESP32 running the OpenHydronic firmware.

discovery_confirm.title: OpenHydronic board found
discovery_confirm.description: Add {name} ({host})? The next step maps its relays to zones. If the board is already set up in the ESPHome integration, they are filled in for you.

not_adopted.title: Add the board to ESPHome first
not_adopted.description: {name} is not in Home Assistant's ESPHome integration yet, and that is where its relays come from. Add it under Settings, Devices & services, then press Check again. Or add the board now and map its zones later.

no_zones.title: The board has not reported its relays
no_zones.description: ESPHome knows {name}, but its relays have not appeared yet. Give it a minute and check again, or add the board now and map its zones later.

zones.title: Map your zones
zones.description: {name} has {count} relays. Pick a temperature sensor for every relay that heats a room and leave the others empty: a relay with no sensor does not become a zone. Have your room sensors in Home Assistant first. You can map the rest later in Configure.

data_description.master_choice: What switches your boiler or circulator. Leave it on None if nothing does, or if this board does not control it. If you choose The board switches it, the board keeps its master relay for that (relay 8 on the published firmware): leave that relay without a sensor.
data_description.master_entity: Only for Another switch in Home Assistant. A switch picked here counts as that answer.

air_purge.name: Air purge
air_purge.description: Opens every valve with the circulator running to bleed trapped air.

run_anti_seize.name: Run anti-seize routine
run_anti_seize.description: Cycles every relay so actuators do not seize.

emergency_stop.name: Emergency stop
emergency_stop.description: Closes every valve and stops the circulator immediately, ignoring the minimum cycle timers.

zones_unmapped.title: {name} has relays but no zones
zones_unmapped.description: Home Assistant has found the relays of {name}, but nothing uses them yet. Open the OpenHydronic entry, choose Configure, then Add the board's relays as zones.

confirm.title: Set a password for {name}
confirm.description: The board answers to admin / admin on its own page, and anyone on your network can open its valves or load firmware. Choose a password of 8 to 64 characters: letters, digits, spaces and the symbols of an English keyboard, no accents. It protects the board's page and its firmware updates, and the user stays admin.

error.password_chars: Use only letters, digits, spaces and the symbols of an English keyboard, no accents.
error.password_failed: The board did not take it. Check that it is online and connected to your network, then try again.
